title: Per-route accumulator reset on epoch boundary causing brief unlimited window
creator: Marcos Alvarez
description: Users intermittently see apparent unlimited throughput for a small window (10-30s) on specific routes following epoch boundary alignments. This leads to temporary billing undercount for some orgs and confusing client-side behavior (requests accepted when they should be throttled). The issue is reproducible in staging when shard clocks are aligned across replicas and when many in-flight allocations land near epoch transitions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy rateengine with 4 shards and enable per-route accumulator flag in staging
2) Warm load generator against /v1/generate-route with sustained RPS approximating burst threshold
3) Force epoch boundary by aligning shard timers (test helper: scripts/sync_epoch.sh) and continue load across boundary
4) Observe accepted requests count vs expected denies in Grafana rate-engine/accumulator-compare dashboard
5) Capture evaluator logs from shard nodes and API gateway for the 60s window around the boundary
observed_behavior: At epoch boundary the per-route accumulator on each shard resets locally then reconciles via async snapshot. During reconciliation, the policy evaluator sometimes treats negative reconciliation deltas as >0 tokens remaining, resulting in a temporary permissive state where requests that should have been throttled are allowed. Billing reports show undercount for affected orgs for the reconciliation period.
expected_behavior: Accumulators should never produce a transient permissive state during epoch alignment. Either reconciled deltas must be applied atomically with a conservative deny-by-default behavior until reconciliation confirms remaining credits, or a protective zero-window should be applied to prevent overserve.
root_cause_summary: The accumulator reset flow zeroes local counters at epoch rollover and then applies remote reconciled deltas via a vector of in-flight allocations. A race between in-flight token allocations and the reconciliation patch can cause signed integer underflow in the local remaining-credit field which the evaluator treats as a large unsigned value (due to historic typed conversion in C++ shard code), effectively granting large remaining capacity for a short period.
workaround: Patch deploy: enable safe-rollover-guard=true on staging/hosted to force deny-until-confirmed behavior (temporary configuration toggle)
Operational: stagger shard epoch timers by 5s to avoid simultaneous zeroing across shards in the short term
mitigation_plan: 1) Fix typed conversion and add saturation arithmetic in accumulator delta application to prevent underflow (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/4219)
2) Add a 'deny-until-reconciled' conservative flag that prevents granting tokens until reconciled state is applied for an epoch transition
3) Add end-to-end integration test that simulates synchronized epoch boundaries with high in-flight allocation and verifies no permissive window
4) Backfill billing sampler to recalculate undercounted usage during affected windows and issue adjustments for impacted customers
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering epoch boundary race pass in CI
Staging run with synchronized shard timers shows zero permissive acceptances for 1 hour run at previous failing load pattern
PR code review sign-off from runtime and billing teams
Post-deploy monitoring dashboard shows reconciled delta deltas are non-negative and no underflow events logged
rollout_plan: Canary deploy fixed runtime to 10% of shards in staging first
Run 6-hour stress with test harness and validate metrics: accepted/denied ratio, accumulator-delta-signature histogram
Promote to hosted region us-east-1 in staged canary (10% traffic) for 2 hours; if stable, 50% for 1 hour; then global
Run billing reconciliation job after global rollout to identify affected windows and prepare credits/invoices as needed
monitoring_after_rollout: New grafana panels: accumulator-underflow-rate, epoch-reconcile-latency, per-route-temporary-accepts
Audit log sample: log all reconciliation patches applied for 1 week
notes: This differs from previous 'burst credit duplication' issues because root cause is arithmetic underflow + epoch simultaneity, not duplicate application of credits.
Related historical tickets: ENG-82712 (async-credit-burn-race) provides context on in-flight allocation races but was resolved using a different guard pattern.
Billing team lead (J. O'Neill) to draft customer comms for any impacted high-volume customers
